activities.name: Box breathing
activities.desc: Inhale 4 counts, hold 4, exhale 4, hold 4. Repeat 3 times. Instantly calms the nervous system.

activities.name: Posture rebalancing
activities.desc: Stand or sit tall. Roll your shoulders back and down, gently lift the crown of your head, and take three slow breaths in the new alignment.

activities.name: Self-hug
activities.desc: Wrap your arms around yourself and squeeze firmly. Hold for 30 seconds, breathing slowly. A real physical signal of safety to your body.

activities.name: Shoulder rub
activities.desc: Use your opposite hand to firmly knead the top of each shoulder and the back of your neck. Spend 30 seconds each side.

activities.name: Cold water on wrists
activities.desc: Run cold water over the inside of your wrists and behind your ears for 30 seconds. Activates the vagus nerve.

categories.title: 5 min chillout
categories.sub: Just enough to shift the state

activities.name: Observing scenery
activities.desc: Go to a window or step outside. Look at whatever is in front of you — sky, trees, street — without agenda. Let your eyes go soft and wide.

activities.name: Watch a short relaxation video
activities.desc: Put on a 5-minute guided breathwork, nature sounds, or body scan video. Lie down if you can. Just receive it.

activities.name: Quick tai chi
activities.desc: A slow, flowing sequence of arm circles, weight shifts and gentle turns. No experience needed — move as slowly as feels natural.

activities.name: Play 5 min online game
activities.desc: Pick something light and absorbing — a word game, puzzle or casual game. Enough to redirect your mind without a big commitment.

activities.name: Shaking it out
activities.desc: Stand up and shake your hands, arms, then whole body loosely for 2–3 minutes. Releases stored physical tension.

activities.name: Yin stretch — hips & spine
activities.desc: Child's pose (2 min), seated spinal twist each side (2 min), legs up the wall (4 min). Slow, passive holds.

activities.name: Self-acupressure
activities.desc: Press firmly on the space between your thumb and index finger (He Gu point). Hold 30–60 sec each hand. Then press the point 3 finger-widths below your kneecap.

activities.name: Slow walking meditation
activities.desc: Walk very slowly indoors or outside. Feel each foot make contact with the ground. No destination, no pace.

activities.name: Listen to favourite tunes
activities.desc: Put on a song or two that you genuinely love. Sit or lie down. Let the music be the only thing happening.

activities.name: Mindful spreadeagle
activities.desc: Lie flat on your back, arms and legs wide. Close your eyes. Feel every point of contact between your body and the floor. Breathe and do absolutely nothing.

categories.title: 20 min deep retune
categories.sub: When you need a real reset

activities.name: Full body stretching flow
activities.desc: A slow, unguided sequence: neck rolls, chest opener, forward fold, hip flexor stretch, pigeon pose, supine twist, savasana. Hold each 1–2 minutes.

activities.name: Mindful strolling
activities.desc: Head outside with no destination. Walk at whatever pace feels right. Notice what you see, hear and smell. No podcasts, no phone.

activities.name: Watch comedy
activities.desc: Put on a short stand-up clip or a favourite funny show. Laughter is genuinely decompressive — let yourself enjoy it without guilt.

activities.name: Play instrument
activities.desc: Pick up whatever you play and just explore — pieces you know well, improvise, or noodle freely. No practising, no pressure. Just the feel of it.

activities.name: Tidy up
activities.desc: Pick one small area — a desk, a bench, a shelf. Slow, deliberate tidying can be deeply calming. Physical order, mental order.

activities.name: Time for solitude
activities.desc: Carve out unstructured time alone — no agenda, no screens unless you want them. Read, wander, sit in the garden, stare at the ceiling. Just be.

activities.name: Group nature walk
activities.desc: Organise a walk with people you like in a park, bushland or along the water. Conversation plus movement plus nature is a powerful combination.

activities.name: Evening out
activities.desc: Get out of the house — dinner, a gallery, live music, a film. A change of scene and a bit of occasion can shift your entire register.

activities.name: Watch a movie
activities.desc: Pick something you've been meaning to watch. Make it comfortable — snacks, blanket, lights low. Full commitment, no multitasking.

activities.name: Catch up with a friend
activities.desc: Call or meet someone you actually feel good around. Not to solve anything — just to connect, laugh and be known by someone.
